subject: RE: Pricing exhibit — proposed stabilization language and order-form clarifications
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>

Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-10T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing exhibit — suggested language for price bands

Alex / Grace,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement had a quick pass at the order form and sent back one suggested change we'd like to discuss: rather than a fixed "cap / floor" on per-token pricing tied to monthly usage, we'd prefer a "price stabilization band" that softens the step changes as usage grows or shrinks.

High level asks:
- Can Redwood accept a banded pricing approach (e.g., $0.006–$0.008 for 0–10M tokens, $0.005–$0.007 for 10–50M) with the lower bound guaranteed and the upper bound acting as an overage cushion?
- How would that interact with reserved capacity (we're targeting Dedicated) and committed discounts — do committed spend discounts apply to the lower bound only or to billed tokens net of stabilization?

I've attached our redline to Exhibit A (simple markup). Our GC also asked for a fallback if the model family is changed during the term.

Appreciate a quick note on what's workable this week — procurement is on a tight timeline for our Q4 renewal window.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Lee
Sr. Sourcing Manager, Acme Retail
Attachments: acme-exhibitA-redline.pdf (pdf)

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear ask and the redline. High level response: we can support a stabilization band conceptally, but we need to be prescriptive on (1) how the lower-bound guaranteed rate applies when you hit committed thresholds, (2) how overages are billed in months exceeding committed capacity, and (3) the model-family fallback you mentioned.

Quick answers:
- Committed discount applies to billed usage up to the committed tokens at the lower-bound rate. If you exceed committed tokens in a billing month, the overage will bill at the applicable upper-band rate unless a negotiated overage discount is added to the order form.
- For Dedicated, we can offer a hybrid approach: committed throughput priced at the lower bound; burst/overage priced at the upper bound but capped monthly to protect against runaway bills.
- For model-family changes, we propose language that maps pricing by model family equivalence classes (e.g., Llama-v2-equivalent) and includes a 60-day notice + temporary price alignment during migration.

I've attached our draft redline to Exhibit A and a clean Order Form v2 reflecting the hybrid committed/burst rows. Grace — would you and Laura take the legal redlines below and flag any must-not language?

Next steps:
1) Grace/legal run-through (Alex will consolidate)
2) If agreed, we prepare a DocuSign packet and a final summary of token buckets + expected monthly billing for your finance team.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min sync if easier.

Best,
Alex Martinez

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-11T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit — suggested language for price bands (legal comments)

Alex / Laura —

Quick legal take on Jordan's proposed banded approach. I reviewed the draft exhibit and marked a few material points in our redline:

1) "Lower bound guaranteed" — we should avoid absolute language that would prevent us from adjusting prices during an extraordinary event (e.g., hardware price shock). Propose: "Lower bound applies to billed usage up to committed tokens, subject to extraordinary cost adjustments with 90 days' notice."

2) "Upper bound as overage cushion" — fine, but need a monthly cap and a clear definition of "billed tokens" to avoid prefix-cache double-counting. Suggest a monthly overage cap equal to 2x the committed bucket unless otherwise negotiated.

3) "Model-family fallback" — propose: pricing mapped to "model families" and a discrete equivalence table in Exhibit A. If Redwood deprecates a model, Redwood will migrate customers to a same-or-better family at no less favorable pricing for 60 days; thereafter, pricing will align to the new family's published exhibit.

4) "Audit & usage disputes" — add 30-day dispute window and rights to audit a trailing 6 months via CSV export; any billing corrections back to 90 days. (This is standard for procurement teams.)

5) "Change order & service credits" — include a small service-credit remedy (up to one month of committed fees pro-rata) for sustained SLA misses that materially affect committed throughput.

I've kept the redlines tight — attached. If we want to present to Acme, we should call out the tradeoffs (lower guaranteed rate vs. commitment size) and propose one or two tiered options (conservative, aggressive) with sample spend math.

- Grace
Grace O'Connor
Head of Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
Attachment: legal-exhibit-comments.pdf (pdf)

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit — technical notes on billing semantics

Looping in a few technical clarifications that will matter for the sample math and the definition of "billed tokens":

1) Prefix/KV cache: if Acme uses a lot of short repeated prompts, our prefix cache can reduce billed tokens for identical continuations — billed tokens are measured post-cache. We should define billed tokens as "tokens submitted to the model execution engine after cache normalization."

2) Dedicated throughput vs. burst: Dedicated reservations are provisioned capacity (vCPU/GPU) that convert to committed token buckets via an agreed formula (we include an appendix that converts throughput to expected tokens per minute based on your request distribution).

3) Measurement lag & dispute CSV: we emit hourly CSV logs and can provide a 6-month usage export; differences in rounding are typically <0.1% but will be called out.

I'll prepare the sample invoice numbers with two bundling options (conservative commitments / aggressive commitments) and flag where bandwidth or caching materially changes the outcome.

- Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Product Manager, Serving Runtime
